actors.name: Transitional Government of Sudan

strength.note: KAS estimate of total SAF strength during the war. Separate allied commands and personnel immediately deployable on 1 January are not measured.

laws.name: Military-led transitional executive
laws.note: The February 2025 amendment extended the transition and strengthened the Transitional Sovereignty Council. Kamil Idris headed an appointed cabinet.

laws.name: Wartime public finances
laws.note: Government budget guidance cites emergency financial arrangements, the amended constitutional document and the Juba Peace Agreement.

objectives: Reestablish central administration across Sudan
Restore public services in recaptured areas

actors.name: Sudan Founding Alliance (Tasis)

strength.note: KAS cites the prewar RSF scale. Wartime mobilization and losses make this a historical reference. Independent Tasis partners keep separate pools.

laws.name: Secular, decentralized government
laws.note: Articles 4–5 establish a secular state and political, administrative, legal and financial decentralization. These are the rival government's constitutional commitments.

laws.name: Equal citizenship and freedom of belief
laws.note: Articles 4 and 29 set out equal citizenship and freedom of thought, belief and worship. The charter does not establish whether the guarantees were enforced.

laws.name: Wartime transitional administration
laws.note: Article 45 places the pre-transitional period before the official end of the wars. A foundational transition follows.

laws.name: Independent media and public access to information
laws.note: Articles 30–31 guarantee independent print and electronic media and internet access to information, with limited statutory exceptions. This is a charter commitment.

laws.name: Limits on capital punishment
laws.note: Article 27 limits capital punishment to the most serious crimes and includes protections for minors, older people, and pregnant or nursing women.

laws.name: Free basic education
laws.note: Article 36 calls for free, compulsory, pluralistic basic education. The game uses lower secondary as the closest level without assigning additional attendance ages.

objectives: Maintain the rival administration based in Nyala
Pursue the alliance's stated decentralized constitutional settlement

actors.name: Darfur Joint Forces
objectives: Preserve a role for Darfuri signatories of the Juba Peace Agreement

actors.name: Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North (al-Hilu faction)
objectives: Keep regional self-government in its Nuba Mountains areas
Advance the secular and decentralized terms of the Tasis charter

actors.name: Sudan Liberation Army (Abdel Wahid al-Nur faction)
State Security and Peace Commission

strength.note: USCIRF estimates the armed forces in 2024. IISS reports 60,000–80,000 cumulative conscript intakes by August 2025. These figures measure different populations and are not added.

laws.name: Military-led interim government
laws.note: The SSPC was the ruling military commission at the cutoff. The 2008 constitution reserved 25 percent of the seats in each national chamber for the military when parliament sat.

laws.name: Restricted political participation
laws.note: The first phase of military-run voting had taken place on 28 December. Major opponents were excluded and independent media faced restrictions.

laws.name: People's Military Service Law
laws.note: The military began enforcing compulsory service in 2024. The game uses the standard two-year term.

laws.name: Regional martial law
laws.note: The military lifted the nationwide state of emergency in July and said it would maintain martial law in 63 townships.

objectives: Maintain the military's role in the national executive
Extend control over contested regions

actors.name: National Unity Government

strength.note: IISS distinguishes allied PDF from independent local defence forces. 2025 field research documents fragmented command. The game pool covers the NUG-linked core.

laws.name: Federal Democracy Charter
laws.note: The charter provides interim institutions and a road map for replacing the 2008 constitution with a federal democratic union. Its geographic implementation is uneven.

laws.name: Civilian authority and federal self-government
laws.note: The interim NUG is tasked with building a federal democratic union in consultation with political parties, ethnic organizations and civil society.

laws.name: People's Police Force Law
laws.note: The CRPH enacted the law for the NUG's administration. Local enforcement varies.

laws.name: Union Taxation Law, 2023
laws.note: The CRPH enacted the law for its administration. It applies in the game to areas where the NUG administers taxation.

objectives: End military rule
Build a federal democratic union with participating regions and ethnic organizations

actors.name: United League of Arakan / Arakan Army

strength.note: ISP's estimate gives the lower bound. The Center for Arakan Studies gave a higher estimate. These are broad faction totals and not independent confirmation of deployed personnel.

laws.name: Arakan regional administration
laws.note: The ULA built separate regional governing institutions across much of Rakhine. Its authority and administration are represented where evidenced.

objectives: Maintain separate regional administration in Rakhine
Seek substantially greater self-government

actors.name: Kachin Independence Organization / Kachin Independence Army

strength.note: ISP estimate for the KIO/KIA. Independent partners retain their own force identities.

objectives: Maintain Kachin self-government and its own political institutions

actors.name: Karen National Union / Karen National Liberation Army

strength.note: ISP estimate for KNU/KNLA. The separate game pool represents a fraction of that broad organization-wide figure.

laws.name: Karen National Union constitution
laws.note: The KNU's own constitution, amended in 2023, sets out how it administers its areas. It seeks Karen self-determination within a democratic federal union.

objectives: Secure Karen self-determination
Build a federal union based on democracy

actors.name: Chin National Front / Chin National Army
objectives: Pursue Chin autonomy and a federal democratic settlement

actors.name: Chin National Organization / Chin National Defence Force
objectives: Maintain independent Chin resistance and regional representation

actors.name: Karenni National Progressive Party / Karenni Army
objectives: Pursue Karenni self-determination and a federal democratic settlement

actors.name: Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army
objectives: Preserve Kokang self-administration under the January 2025 ceasefire

actors.name: Palaung State Liberation Front / Ta'ang National Liberation Army
objectives: Preserve Ta'ang self-administration under the October 2025 ceasefire

actors.name: United Wa State Party / United Wa State Army
objectives: Preserve de facto Wa autonomy

conflicts.name: Sudanese Civil War

regions.name: Khartoum
regions.note: The SAF recaptured Khartoum in 2025. The province begins under government military control.

regions.name: Red Sea
regions.note: Port Sudan remained the wartime government seat at the cutoff.

regions.name: Southern Darfur
regions.note: Nyala is the seat of the rival administration.

regions.name: North Darfur
regions.note: The RSF took El Fasher in October. Control across the whole game region is mixed.

regions.name: Central Darfur
regions.note: The SLA/AW is a separate, non-aligned actor in Jebel Marra.

regions.name: South Kordufan
regions.note: The SAF, RSF and SPLM-N (al-Hilu) hold different areas. The game map has no separate West Kordofan province.

regions.name: North Kordufan
regions.note: The game region includes territory under competing control.

conflicts.note: War began on 15 April 2023. The RSF leads the rival Sudan Founding Alliance. The African Union rejected recognition of its parallel government. Displacement, famine and restricted humanitarian access affect civilians independently of territory control.

conflicts.name: Myanmar Civil War: National Unity Government

regions.name: Sagaing
regions.note: NUG-linked PDF and independent local defence groups hold or administer parts of this game region. Military authorities retain other areas.

regions.name: Magway
regions.note: Local resistance and military government control vary across the region.

regions.name: Mandalay
regions.note: Mandalay city remains under the military administration. Parts of the larger game region are contested.

conflicts.note: The military seized power in February 2021. At the cutoff, the SSPC retained central state institutions. The NUG had its own armed networks and local partners. Ethnic forces and regional administrations have their own political authority and do not share one national command.

conflicts.name: Myanmar Civil War: Arakan

regions.name: Chin
regions.note: The United League of Arakan administered Paletwa town. The game province includes territory governed by several other authorities.

regions.name: Rakhine
regions.note: The ULA administered much of Rakhine. The military continued to hold some areas, including Sittwe. This game region combines multiple local jurisdictions.

conflicts.note: The Arakan Army and its political wing operate independently of the National Unity Government.

regions.name: Kachin
regions.note: The KIO administered parts of Kachin. Military authorities retained other areas.

regions.name: Kayin
regions.note: The KNU administered areas alongside a wider patchwork of military and other Karen authorities.

regions.name: Chin
regions.note: Chin resistance and governing groups include distinct organizations. The whole game region is not assigned to any one organization.

regions.name: Kayah
regions.note: The Karenni Army, Karenni Nationalities Defence Force and other regional groups operate in a patchwork with military-controlled territory.

conflicts.name: Myanmar Civil War: Chin National Defence Force

regions.name: Chin
regions.note: The CNDF is the armed wing of the Chin National Organization. It operates independently of the Chin National Front.

conflicts.name: Myanmar: Kokang Ceasefire

regions.name: Shan
regions.note: Kokang is one part of a larger province. The ceasefire is bilateral and does not decide control across Shan.

conflicts.note: The MNDAA and Myanmar military reached a China-mediated ceasefire effective 18 January 2025.

conflicts.name: Myanmar: Ta'ang Ceasefire

regions.name: Shan
regions.note: Ta'ang-administered areas share the game region with several distinct authorities, including Wa, Kokang and the central military government.

conflicts.note: The TNLA announced a China-mediated ceasefire effective 29 October 2025. Fighting elsewhere in Myanmar remained active.
